nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, d$ be natural numbers and put $s_1 = ab + 1$, $s_2 = ac + 1$, $s_3 = ad + 1$, $s_4 = bc + 1$, $s_5 = bd + 1$, $s_6 = cd + 1$. For indices $i, j$ let $t_{ij}$ be the integer $(s_j - s_i) / \gcd(s_j, s_i)$. Then $a \mid \gcd(t_{12}, t_{13}, t_{23})$, $b \mid \gcd(t_{14}, t_{15}, t_{45})$, $c \mid \gcd(t_{24}, t_{26}, t_{46})$ and $d \mid \gcd(t_{35}, t_{36}, t_{56})$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ divide gcds of reduced differences

nodes.summary: The set $\{1, 3\}$ is a $\{2\}$-Diophantine tuple, since $1 \cdot 3 + 1 = 2^2$.
nodes.title: $(1, 3)$ is a $\{2\}$-Diophantine pair

nodes.summary: The set $\{1, 3, 8\}$ is a $\{2, 3, 5\}$-Diophantine tuple, since $1 \cdot 3 + 1 = 2^2$, $1 \cdot 8 + 1 = 3^2$ and $3 \cdot 8 + 1 = 5^2$.
nodes.title: $(1, 3, 8)$ is a $\{2, 3, 5\}$-Diophantine triple

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers. A finite set $s$ of natural numbers is an $S$-Diophantine tuple if all its elements are positive and, for all distinct $a, b \in s$, every prime factor of $ab + 1$ lies in $S$. A tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_m)$ of distinct positive integers is encoded by the set of its entries, which has $m$ elements.
nodes.title: $S$-Diophantine tuples

nodes.summary: Let $p \ne q$ be primes with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ or $q \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. Then no four-element set of natural numbers is a $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine tuple; that is, there is no $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine quadruple.
nodes.title: No $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine quadruple when $p$ or $q$ is $3$ modulo $4$

nodes.summary: Let $p < q$ be primes. Then no five-element set of natural numbers is a $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine tuple; that is, there is no $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine quintuple.
nodes.title: There is no $\{p, q\}$-Diophantine quintuple

nodes.summary: Let $p \ne q$ be odd primes and let $a, b, c, d$ be integers with $0 < a < b < c < d$. Then there are no natural numbers $\beta_1, \alpha_4, \beta_4, \alpha_2, \alpha_5, \alpha_3, \beta_3, \beta_6$ with $ab + 1 = q^{\beta_1}$, $bc + 1 = p^{\alpha_4} q^{\beta_4}$, $ac + 1 = p^{\alpha_2}$, $bd + 1 = p^{\alpha_5}$, $ad + 1 = p^{\alpha_3} q^{\beta_3}$ and $cd + 1 = q^{\beta_6}$.
nodes.title: The Szalay–Ziegler system (4) has no solutions

nodes.summary: If $a < b < c$ are positive integers, then $ac + 1$ does not divide $bc + 1$.
nodes.title: $ac + 1$ does not divide $bc + 1$

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $a, b, c, d$ natural numbers. Put $s_1 = ab + 1$, $s_2 = ac + 1$, $s_3 = ad + 1$, $s_4 = bc + 1$, $s_5 = bd + 1$, $s_6 = cd + 1$, and let $v_i$ be the $\ell$-adic valuation of $s_i$. Then in each of the tuples $(v_2, v_3, v_4, v_5)$, $(v_1, v_2, v_5, v_6)$ and $(v_1, v_3, v_4, v_6)$ the minimum value occurs at two different positions.
nodes.title: The two smallest valuations coincide

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
